watchlist.title: My watchlist
watchlist.what: Tickers you chose to follow, checked every day: how the price is moving, how far it is from its high of the past year, the most relevant recent headline, and whether investors or engineers are talking about it.
watchlist.careful: Watching a stock closely makes every move feel important. Most daily moves are noise - the one-month change and the headline tell you far more than today's number.

trending.title: Trending right now
trending.what: The stocks individual investors are talking about most today, on Stocktwits and Reddit, with a summary of what the conversation is about.
trending.careful: Trending means people are arguing about it, not that it is a good investment. Stocks often trend because something just went very right or very wrong - and by the time a stock is trending, the news is already in the price.

dipping.title: Popular, but falling
dipping.what: Well-known or much-discussed stocks that are well below their highest price of the past year, or that dropped sharply in the last month.
dipping.careful: A dip is not automatically a discount. Prices usually fall for a reason - a weak earnings report, a lost customer, a bigger worry about the industry. Find out why before assuming it will bounce back; plenty of stocks never return to their old high.

compare.title: Compare
compare.what: What you pay for each company next to what it earns - the same table for a chip giant, a burger chain, a cloud company that loses money and a car maker priced on its future, plus your watchlist. Tap a row for its full value card.
compare.careful: A high multiple is not 'expensive' and a low one is not 'cheap'. A high P/E means the price expects a lot of growth; always read it next to the growth rate. No single number decides anything.

tech.title: Popular with tech people
tech.what: Companies software engineers are writing about on Hacker News this month - mostly businesses that sell to developers and other companies, so most people have never heard of them - and that the retail stock forums are not talking about. Most come from a hand-picked list of tech companies. Ones marked "found automatically" come from a search of every listed tech company and recent tech IPO - check the headline shown to confirm it is really about the company.
tech.careful: Engineers talk about products, outages and technology, not about whether a stock is fairly priced. A company can have a product developers love and still be a poor investment - or already be priced as if everyone knows how good it is.

Traders are debating potential liability and contract fallout, while others argue LHX is being scapegoated and see the selloff as a buying opportunity.

trending.name: Delta Air Lines
trending.why: A nationwide FAA air-traffic communications outage triggered a ground stop that disrupted thousands of flights, drawing concern about cancellations, operating costs and near-term pressure on Delta and other airlines. Traders disagree on whether the disruption is a temporary hit now that the stop has been lifted or a more lasting earnings risk; claims of a cyberattack or AI involvement remain speculation.

trending.name: BlackRock
trending.why: BlackRocks latest quarterly report beat adjusted earnings and revenue expectations, with strong client inflows and record assets under management driving bullish reactions and analyst upgrades. Some traders question the quality of the results, citing the gap between GAAP and adjusted earnings, while others remain wary of fee pressure and private-credit exposure.

trending.name: MoonLake Immunotherapeutics
trending.why: MoonLakes pending FDA decision on whether to accept its sonelokimab application for hidradenitis suppurativa is the main focus, with traders also watching for a possible priority review. Bulls point to the drugs clinical data and potential pharma interest, while bears emphasize regulatory risk and concerns about launching alone, cash burn, and future dilution.

trending.name: United Airlines
trending.why: A nationwide FAA ground stop after air-traffic-control communications failures is driving attention, with mass cancellations and delays weighing on airline shares. Traders debate whether the disruption is a temporary setback that could prompt a rebound or a sign of broader infrastructure problems; cyberattack and AI theories remain unverified.

trending.name: Lyft
trending.why: Lyfts Q3 results are the main focus, with a revenue and GAAP earnings miss alongside a legal, tax and regulatory reserve charge, while bookings and adjusted profitability improved. Traders are split between concern over the headline miss and optimism about underlying growth and the companys outlook.

trending.name: Comfort Systems USA
trending.why: Comfort Systems exposure to AI data-center construction is driving discussion, with traders weighing strong earnings and a record backlog against concerns that financing delays, project slippage, and policy risks could slow spending and backlog conversion. The recent rebound has prompted dip-buying, but skepticism remains about whether the booked work will translate into sustained revenue.
